previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with fevers, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and shortness of breath. Imaging revealed a hypodense lesion in the upper pole of the right kidney with perinephric stranding, concerning for a renal or perinephric abscess. She was started on IV pip/tazo and vancomycin, with vancomycin administered slowly due to a history of Red Man syndrome. Blood cultures were negative. An abdominal ultrasound confirmed a focal hypoechoic lesion consistent with bacterial nephritis but no drainable collection. Her respiratory symptoms improved after hemodialysis, attributed to volume overload. She remained afebrile with stable pain controlled on hydromorphone. She was discharged on oral ciprofloxacin and IV vancomycin to be administered during outpatient hemodialysis for a 14-day course, with instructions to monitor for fever and obtain a follow-up ultrasound.

THREE VIEWS OF BOTH HANDS

INDICATION:  Lupus and fevers, assess for flare.

COMPARISON:  Two hand radiographs, ___.

FINDINGS:

RIGHT HAND:  There has been progression in arthropathy at the distal
interphalangeal joints of the second through fifth fingers with increased
predominantly central erosion.  Mild volar subluxation of the distal phalanx
of the fourth digit is noted.  No chondrocalcinosis is seen. 
Metacarpophalangeal joints are within normal limits with no evidence of
subluxation or erosion.  Bones appear mildly osteopenic.

LEFT HAND:

Bones appear osteopenic.  There is arthropathy at the distal interphalangeal
joints of the second through fifth digits, which is relatively similar to the
prior examination in ___, joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation in
addition to volar subluxation of the distal phalanx of the fifth and second
digits.  Bones are osteopenic.  No chondrocalcinosis is seen.  No
metacarpophalangeal erosion or subluxation is seen.  No fracture is
demonstrated.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Similar appearance of the left hand with distal interphalangeal joint
second through fifth digit arthropathy characterized by joint space narrowing
and osteophyte formation with some subluxation.
2.  Progression over a five-year period of the right hand with increased
second through fifth digit arthropathy with joint space narrowing, osteophyte
formation, and central erosion and with features suggesting erosive
osteoarthritis.  No metacarpophalangeal joint subluxation is evident.

INDICATION:  ___ female with lupus, fever, abdominal pain, and
elevated LFT and lipase.  Patient also has a new rash and mild dyspnea on
exertion.  Question source of fever.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior CTs, most recently ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired from the thoracic inlet through the
pubic symphysis following administration of intravenous and oral contrast,
with multiplanar reformations.

CT CHEST:  Linear right upper lobe and left lower lobe scarring appear
unchanged since at least ___.   Since ___, there has been
interval development of small bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than
left.  Small air-filled lobules at the margin of collapsed right lower lobe
(2, 47), may suggest residual pulmonary tissue.  The heart is enlarged, with
trace pericardial effusion.  Multivessel coronary arterial disease and aortic
valve calcifications are noted.

CT ABDOMEN:  There is no focal liver lesion.  There is no biliary dilatation.
The gallbladder is surgically absent.  A 1.4 x 0.9 cm hypoattenuating splenic
lesion appears unchanged, which could represent a cyst or hemangioma. 
Scattered calcifications within the spleen suggest prior granulomatous
disease.  A splenule, pancreas, and adrenal glands appear within normal
limits.  Bilateral kidneys are miniscule in size but demonstrate symmetric
nephrograms.  There is no hydronephrosis or hydroureter. Multiple
subcentimeter renal hypodensities are too small to fully characterize but
unchanged.  There is no abnormal collection within the abdomen.  

The stomach, duodenum, small and large bowel loops are normal in caliber. 
There is normal contrast progression to the level of the rectum.  There is
omental infarct in the right lower quadrant (2, 83), unchanged since at least
___, of doubtful clinical significance.  Multiple
borderline-sized retroperitoneal lymph nodes are unchanged.  For example, a
paraaortic lymph node at the level of the kidneys on the left measures 1.6 x
0.7 cm.  An antecaval lymph node measures 1.7 x 0.8 cm (2, 76).  These are
nonspecific.  There is no free air or free fluid.

CT PELVIS:  Assessment of pelvic structures is limited by significant streak
metal artifacts from a right hemiarthroplasty.  The bladder appears collapsed.
The rectum and distal colon are within normal limits.  There is no inguinal or
pelvic lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria.  Multiple right iliac fossa clips
are redemonstrated, consistent with post surgical changes of prior resection
of a failed renal transplant.  There is no free fluid within the pelvis.

BONE WINDOWS:  Diffusely sclerotic and mottled appearance of osseous
structures is consistent with renal osteodystrophy.  Right total hip
arthroplasty is in place.  An intervertebral ossicle at the level of L2-3 is
unchanged.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Small bilateral pleural effusions are new since ___.
2.  No CT evidence of acute intra-abdominal process, including pancreatitis,
pyelonephritis, renal abscess, or colitis.
3.  Unchanged splenic lesion, likely a cyst or hemangioma.
4.  Renal osteodystrophy.
